question.leadin: A powerful family that ruled this city included men like Lorezno the Magnificent.
question.text: Name this Italian city once ruled by the Medici family. This city is the most populous one in Tuscany.
question.clue: This city was the site of the Pazzi conspiracy, and much of its art and literature was destroyed in the Bonfire of the Vanities, ordered by the monk Savonarola.

swap.leadin: Name the following Italian cities that were powerful during the Middle Ages and Renaissance.
swap.text: Under the Doge Enrico Dandolo, this city provided support for troops during the Fourth Crusade.
swap.clue: Its first patron saint was Theodore, but in 828 it obtained the relics of Saint Mark.

question.leadin: While in exile, this man fought in Uruguay.
question.text: Name this revolutionary who led the redshirts of the Expedition of the Thousand against the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.
question.clue: This man led a small force to victory with an uphill bayonet charge at Calatafimi shortly before declaring himself dictator of Sicily.

swap.leadin: This man created the Rome-Berlin Axis with Adolf Hitler.
swap.text: Name this fascist dictator of Italy known as Il Duce, or "the Boss," who took power after a March on Rome.
swap.clue: This politician replaced King Zog with Victor Emmanuel III, and he signed the Lateran Treaty to establish Vatican City.

question.leadin: The Black Death may have first arrived in Europe during the Golden Horde's siege of this city's colony of Caffa.
question.text: Name this Italian city. This maritime republic was the home city of Christopher Columbus.
question.clue: This city was led for much of its history by the Boccanegra family and was the home of admiral Andrea Doria.

swap.leadin: This city originally served as a refugee camp for citizens fleeing from Rome in the 5th century, despite being built on a marsh.
swap.text: Name this Northern Italian city that was its own independent republic from the 7th to 18th centuries. It rivaled the Ottoman Empire for power in the Mediterranean.
swap.answerHtml: Most Serene Republic of Venice [prompt on “Venetian Republic”]
swap.clue: This republic's leaders participated in the annual "Marriage of the Sea" ceremony using the ceremonial raft Bucentaur.

question.text: This leader began the Battle for Births to increase his country's population and strengthen his country's imperial ambitions, which included invasions of Albania and Abyssinia.
question.clue: Futurist artists glorified this leader, who began the Pacification of Libya.

swap.text: This grandfather of Lorenzo de Medici was a skillful statesman during the Italian Renaissance, doing things like keeping councillors in the Florentine Signoria loyal to him. He was succeeded by his son, Piero.
swap.clue: This man persuaded Pope Eugene IV to move the Council of Ferrara to his city, thereby attracting Byzantine wealth and learning.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the reign of Spanish king Charles I.
question.text: At this 1525 battle in northern Italy, Charles' forces recaptured Milan and took Francis I of France as prisoner.
question.clue: The final active Yorkist pretender to the English throne, Richard de la Pole, was killed at this battle.

swap.leadin: After World War II, the Morgan Line split this city's surrounding region into Zone A and Zone B.
swap.text: Name this port city on the Istrian Peninsula that became a "Free Territory" in 1947 to provide a buffer between Yugoslavia and Italy.
swap.clue: This city was the subject of the Treaty of Osimo and was divided by the Morgan Line.

question.text: The League of Cambrai was formed to combat this "Most Serene" Italian republic, which was ruled by "doges." During the Fourth Crusade, Enrico Dandolo, the ruler of this republic, sent crusaders off to siege Constantinople.
question.clue: The Treaty of Campo Formio incorporated this city into Austria, officially ending a republic founded in AD 697.

swap.leadin: This family fled to Venice after Piero the Gouty acceded to all the demands of Charles VIII.
swap.text: Name this Italian family led by men like Cosimo the Elder and Lorenzo the Magnificent.
swap.clue: People with this last name founded a Platonic Academy and were targeted in the Pazzi Conspiracy.

question.leadin: After the failure of this plot, the organizer escaped, was captured, returned to Florence, was tortured, hung, buried, exhumed, thrown into a ditch, dragged through the streets, had his rotting head used as a door knocker, thrown into the Arno, fished out by children, hung from a tree, flogged, and then thrown back into the Arno.
question.text: Name this conspiracy named for the family that organized it and targeted the Medicis.
question.clue: Frederico Montelfeltro likely had a battalion waiting in the hills during this event, which left citizens hanging from the walls of the Palazzo Vecchio and tossed into the Arno river.

swap.text: Many of Boniface's policies were opposed by this medieval faction, which supported the Holy Roman Emperor over the Papacy.
swap.clue: Before winning the battle of Montaperti, this group agreed to the Peace of Constance after it lost the Battle of Legnano, in which it was opposed by the Lombard League.

question.leadin: During this battle, the Arditi Corps earned the nickname "the Caimans of the Piave" for swimming back and forth across the frigid Piave River to carry messages.
question.text: Name this 1918 victory for Armando Diaz, who had replaced Luigi Cadorna the previous year, which led to the Armistice of Villa Giusti.
question.clue: This battle fought exactly one year after Caporetto, which led directly to the Armistice of Villa Giusti. This battle marked the end of World War One on the Italian front.

swap.text: The U.S. 10th Mountain Division was deployed at Riva Ridge at the Battle of Monte Castello in the winter of 1944, during General Clark's assault on this northernmost defensive fortification in Italy.
swap.clue: Brazil's memorial honors members of the Brazilian Expeditionary Force killed trying to capture this Axis defensive position. Operation Olive partially broke through this line defended by Albert Kesselring in Italy's Apennine ("APP-uh-nine") Mountains.

question.text: Dante Alighieri argued against Boniface's position in his treatise De Monarchia, a position which aligned with him being a member of the White branch of this faction, which clashed in Italian politics with the Ghibellines.
question.clue: Charles of Anjou helped this group in establishing themselves in their most important city where the Donati and Cerchi families created "black" and "white" factions, Florence.

swap.text: The forces of this Lombard king were smashed by Charlemagne at the capture of Pavia in 774 CE.
swap.clue: This leader's people were profiled by his rival's courtier, Paul the Deacon, who sought the hand of this man's daughter for his Lord.

question.text: Operation Husky devastated the economy around this city, allowing the bandit Salvatore Giuliano to gain immense power. A series of shoddy Mafia-constructed buildings in this Sicilian city have been called its "sack."
question.clue: This city in which the Maxi Trial took place. Two of the magistrates who organized the Maxi Trial, Giovanni Falcone and Paolo Borsellino, were each murdered by car bombs in this city in 1992.

swap.leadin: [Note to moderator: do not give "Sicily" as part of the answer for part 1] This ruler was to have inherited Jerusalem as part of the contract of his mother Adelaide's marriage to Baldwin I, but Baldwin divorced her, leaving him with nothing.
swap.text: Identify this man who claimed the Apulian region after the death of William of Apulia, the last male descendant of Robert Guiscard.
swap.clue: The Moroccan geographer Muhammad al-Idrisi attended this 12th-century Norman king of Sicily, who combined Byzantine and Arabic influences in the spectacular Palatine Chapel in Palermo.
